history.summary: 24-mixed-scenario-drill.html 7/10. A newcomer would most struggle with the agile and cost words that are used before they are explained, such as sprint, backlog, product owner, earned value and CPI, because the lesson does not name the agile lessons as a prerequisite.

24-mixed-scenario-drill.html 7/10. A newcomer who knows the earlier PMP lessons would follow each question, but would struggle most with the dense Step 4 paragraph, which squeezes three topics and eight names into one block.

24-mixed-scenario-drill.html 7/10. A newcomer would struggle most with the agile words (sprint, velocity, retrospective) that appear without explanation, since the lesson does not list the Agile delivery lessons it relies on.

19-governance-and-flow-questions.html 7/10. A newcomer would mostly struggle with the ITSM vocabulary the questions use, such as principle names, event levels and lifecycle terms, which this practice lesson relies on from earlier lessons rather than explaining.

18-more-question-practice.html 7/10. A newcomer would most struggle with the value terms in Step 3, where output is introduced in a sentence about the two parts of value, so the warranty question is harder than it should be.

15-ai-in-service-management.html 7/10. A newcomer would most likely get stuck on the “AI capability model” mentioned in Step 2, which the lesson names without explaining and points to a place that does not teach it.
18-more-question-practice.html 8/10. A newcomer would mostly get stuck on a few ITSM words the questions use but the lesson never defines, such as "record" and "output".
15-ai-in-service-management.html 7/10.

18-more-question-practice.html 6/10. A newcomer would struggle most with the Learn boxes: they mostly list the answers and point back to earlier lessons, so questions on utility versus warranty, the change types and the four dimensions ask for ideas this page never states.

15-ai-in-service-management.html 7/10. A newcomer would struggle most with the pilot step, where the two checks, the error rate and the fix time, are mixed into one long paragraph, and with an outline and exam reference in the governance step that is never explained.
18-more-question-practice.html 7/10.

15-ai-in-service-management.html 7/10. A newcomer with some AI background would follow most of the lesson, but would get stuck where the three kinds of AI are treated as separate boxes, and where Step 2 points to an outline they do not have.
